newsitem.title: INDIA: Bank of Rajasthan says not seeking ally.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Rajasthan says not seeking ally.

text.p: India's Bank of Rajasthan has given up a plan to seek a foreign partner, and was no longer pursuing an intended alliance with U.S.-based GE Capital Services, its chairman said on Tuesday.
GE Capital Services is a unit of General Electric Capital Corp.

"At one point we thought of having a strategic alliance with one of the leading foreign banks, but the management now thinks that the time is not ripe yet," R.S. Rathore told Reuters in Bhubaneswar, capital of the eastern state of Orissa.

"Unless information technology and human resource development are in good shape, we will not gain from our alliance with foreign banks," said Rathore, who was in Orissa to open the bank's first branch in the state.
Rathore denied a report in some Indian newspapers that the Bangur family, which holds a majority in the bank, planned to sell 20 percent of the bank's equity.

"I am not aware of any plan by the promoters (founders) diluting their stake in the bank. The Bangurs and their family members have roughly about 60 percent of the equity stake in the bank. But at no point of time the issue came up in the board of directors," Rathore said.
